sEn: Recent timeline updates from the AI Futures Project, Paul Christiano, and Dwarkesh Patel suggest superhuman AI researchers may arrive around 2027, so plans presuming more time are inadequate and must include fallbacks.
sZh: AI Futures Project、Paul Christiano 和 Dwarkesh Patel 的最新时间线更新表明，超人类 AI 研究员可能在 2027 年左右出现，因此假定有更多时间的计划都不充分，必须包含后备方案。
absEn: This post reviews recent timeline updates from the AI Futures Project, Paul Christiano, and Dwarkesh Patel, prompted largely by the METR report estimating that AI is roughly doubling the pace of AI research progress at Anthropic. The AI Futures Project now forecasts a Superhuman AI Researcher likely in 2027 and a 35-65% chance of Top-Expert-Dominating AI before 2028, while Christiano warns of meaningful AI takeover risk within 6-12 months and calls for pausing development until alignment and security improve. The author argues these shorter timelines are directionally correct and that a substantial, though under-50%, chance of superintelligence in 2027 should be taken seriously, while cautioning against treating 2027 as a baseline and overreacting. The conclusion is that any plan presuming more time than this is inadequate, yet plans must also include fallbacks if progress is slower or deliberate slowdowns occur, and that more time is needed to make superintelligence likely to go well.
absZh: 本文回顾了 AI Futures Project、Paul Christiano 和 Dwarkesh Patel 近期的时间线更新，这些更新很大程度上由 METR 的报告引发，该报告估计 AI 大约将 Anthropic 的 AI 研究进展速度提高了一倍。AI Futures Project 现在预测超人类 AI 研究员很可能在 2027 年出现，并且到 2028 年之前有 35% 至 65% 的概率出现顶级专家级主导型 AI；而 Christiano 警告称，在 6 至 12 个月内存在重大 AI 接管风险，并呼吁暂停开发，直到对齐与安全状况改善。作者认为这些更短的时间线在方向上是正确的，2027 年出现超级智能的实质性概率（尽管低于 50%）应被认真对待，同时告诫不要将 2027 年视为基线并过度反应。结论是，任何假定拥有比这更多时间的计划都不充分，但计划也必须包含后备方案，以应对进展较慢或有意放缓的情况，并且需要更多时间才能使超级智能更可能顺利发展。

full.secZh: 总体而言的最新进展与现状

paras.en: These updates towards shorter timelines seem directionally correct to me.
paras.zh: 在我看来，这些朝向更短时间线的更新在方向上是正确的。

paras.en: There is a substantial chance that we will see superintelligence developed, that can fully automate AI R&D (SAR) or even do all digital tasks (TED-AI), in 2027. Contra the AI Futures Project, I believe an SAR in 2027 is under 50% to happen, but not so far under 50%. It would be surprising to me but not shocking if we do nothing to slow down and still do not see something close to an SAR by the end of 2028.
paras.zh: 有相当大的可能，我们会在 2027 年看到超级智能被开发出来，它能够完全自动化 AI 研发（SAR），甚至完成所有数字化任务（TED-AI）。与 AI Futures Project 的看法相反，我认为 2027 年出现 SAR 的概率低于 50%，但并没有低到远低于 50% 的程度。如果我们不采取任何减速措施，却到 2028 年底仍未看到接近 SAR 的东西，这会让我感到意外，但不会令我震惊。

paras.en: If you do not have an importantly non-zero chance of the development of superintelligence in 2027, I believe you are making a clear mistake.
paras.zh: 如果你不认为 2027 年开发出超级智能具有重要的非零概率，我认为你显然犯了错误。

paras.en: I worry that some are overreacting, and taking this too far too fast, and treating full superintelligence in 2027 as a baseline scenario rather than a possibility.
paras.zh: 我担心有些人反应过度，把这件事推得太远太快，把 2027 年实现完全超级智能当作基准情景，而不是一种可能性。

paras.en: I reiterate that a lot of these updates feel like people fixing their failure to update previously. Did you need three people from METR in order to believe the things that Anthropic and OpenAI are saying about their internal pace of development? What did you expect a METR report from inside Anthropic to say? Were you not paying attention? Are you this sensitive to the exact set of points on the AECI graph? You should have made a lot of these updates months ago.
paras.zh: 我重申，这些更新中有很多让人觉得是人们终于纠正了自己此前未能及时更新的失误。你难道需要 METR 的三个人才能相信 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 关于其内部研发节奏的说法吗？你指望一份来自 Anthropic 内部的 METR 报告会说些什么？你之前难道没有在关注吗？你对 AECI 图上那组具体数据点就这么敏感吗？这些更新中有很多你几个月前就该做了。

paras.en: Past predictive failures are not what is important. What matters is what happens next.
paras.zh: 过去的预测失败并不重要。重要的是接下来会发生什么。

paras.en: You should be prepared for AI capabilities to advance rapidly in 2027, far more rapidly than in previous years, including the potential for superintelligence and fully strong recursive self-improvement. It is a realistic possibility, although unlikely, that humanity could pass the full point of no return or de facto lose control over the future during 2027, or that life could become seriously disrupted in highly unpleasant ways.
paras.zh: 你应当为 2027 年 AI 能力快速进步做好准备——其速度将远超往年，包括可能出现超级智能和完全强大的递归自我改进。一个现实但可能性不大的情形是：人类可能在 2027 年越过完全不可逆转的临界点，或事实上失去对未来的控制；又或者生活可能以极其令人不快的方式受到严重扰乱。

paras.en: If your plan presumes that it has more time than this, then it is not a good plan.
paras.zh: 如果你的计划假定自己拥有比这更多的时间，那它就不是一个好计划。

paras.en: I have not seen a plan that could make superintelligence likely to go well, if that superintelligence gets built in 2027. We need more time.
paras.zh: 如果超级智能在 2027 年被建造出来，我还没有看到任何一个计划能让它大概率顺利发展。我们需要更多时间。

paras.en: You should also be prepared if recursive self-improvement and superintelligence do not arrive in 2027. There are many things that could impact how fast things go, or what it would take to achieve full RSI or superintelligence. Our observations of the past are noisy. When trying to predict an exponential, small changes in how fast things accelerate can become dramatic differences in when or how things happen.
paras.zh: 你也应当为递归自我改进和超级智能并未在 2027 年到来做好准备。有许多因素可能影响事态发展的速度，或影响实现完全 RSI 或超级智能所需的条件。我们对过去的观察充满噪声。当试图预测指数增长时，加速速度上的微小变化，可能造成事件发生时间或方式的巨大差异。

paras.en: If your plan presumes the crucial events happen in 2027, and fails without a fallback if things take longer than that, then this too is not a good plan.
paras.zh: 如果你的计划假定关键事件会在 2027 年发生，并且一旦事情拖得更久就没有后备方案、从而失败，那么这同样不是一个好计划。

paras.en: It is also possible that we will take collective action, either among the labs or via governments, to limit the rate of capability advances, via pacing of the frontier or even outright pausing development of frontier AI. If so, these timelines become longer.
paras.zh: 另一种可能是，我们会采取集体行动——无论是在各实验室之间，还是通过政府——来限制能力进步的速度，方式包括对前沿模型的发展节奏加以控制，甚至完全暂停前沿 AI 的开发。若果真如此，这些时间线就会变得更长。

paras.en: Different people are talking about different things. Careful ones will be precise.
paras.zh: 不同的人谈论的是不同的事情。谨慎的人会表述精确。

paras.en: Timelines refers to how long we expect it to take to reach various transformational milestones in AI.
paras.zh: 时间线指的是我们预计需要多长时间才能达到人工智能领域的各种变革性里程碑。

paras.en: Typically, these days, what we are measuring is the time until some definition of a form of superintelligence (ASI), typically meaning something of the form ‘AIs that will be able to do approximately all of the things better than you.’
paras.zh: 如今，通常我们衡量的是达到某种定义下的超级智能（ASI）所需的时间，这通常意味着‘能够在几乎所有事情上比你做得更好的人工智能’。

paras.en: We can also talk about particular capabilities. The AI Futures Project, the team behind AI 2027, talks about the Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) that can narrowly take over AI research, and the Top-Expert-Dominating AI (TED-AI) that could automate all white-collar work.
paras.zh: 我们也可以讨论特定的能力。AI Futures Project，即 AI 2027 背后的团队，谈到了能够狭义接管 AI 研究的超人类 AI 研究员（SAR），以及能够自动化所有白领工作的顶级专家主导型 AI（TED-AI）。

paras.en: Because of recursive self-improvement (RSI), once you have an SAR you can use that to build better AIs, so you quickly end up with a TED-AI or a traditional ASI.
paras.zh: 由于递归自我改进（RSI），一旦你拥有了 SAR，你就可以利用它来构建更好的 AI，因此你很快就会得到 TED-AI 或传统的 ASI。

paras.en: We then sometimes talk about any of these, or things in between:
paras.zh: 我们随后有时会讨论上述任一种情况，或介于两者之间的情况：

paras.en: 1. Time until the development of some AI system with particular capabilities.
paras.zh: 1. 直到开发出具备特定能力的某种 AI 系统所需的时间。

paras.en: 2. Time until some impact in the physical world.
paras.zh: 2. 直到在物理世界产生某种影响所需的时间。

paras.en: 3. Time until the Point of No Return, when for practical purposes human decisions can no longer change how things play out from there.
paras.zh: 3. 直到到达不可逆转点（Point of No Return）所需的时间——从那时起，出于实际目的，人类的决策已无法改变事态的走向。

paras.en: 4. Time until AI has taken over AI R&D and humans are functionally out of the loop.
paras.zh: 4. 直到 AI 接管 AI 研发、人类在功能上被排除在循环之外所需的时间。

paras.en: 5. Time until visible AI takeover, where the AIs are clearly in charge.
paras.zh: 5. 直到可见的 AI 接管所需的时间，即 AI 明显处于主导地位。

paras.en: 6. Time until we are each and every one of us actually and physically dead.
paras.zh: 6. 直到我们每一个人都真正且物理意义上死亡所需的时间。

paras.en: There are good reasons to care about all of these timelines.
paras.zh: 我们有充分的理由关注所有这些时间线。

paras.en: Sof 𓋹: to some extent intelligence is being able to patch the ways in which you are not intelligent.
paras.zh: Sof 𓋹：在某种程度上，智能就是能够修补你自身不智能之处的能力。

paras.en: RSI is not technically one singular moment, in the sense that there is not one fixed time at 8:52am on a Tuesday when it happens or starts. It is still highly useful to think of there being a point where RSI has clearly begun in earnest, with humans increasingly out of the loop and the pace of progress accelerating such that we should expect further progress to rapidly continue to accelerate, where progress begets more progress faster, and this is expected to continue for at least what previously would have been many years of progress.
paras.zh: 严格来说，RSI 并非某一个单一时刻，也就是说，并不存在某个固定的时间点——比如周二上午 8:52——它就在那一刻发生或开始。但设想存在一个 RSI 已明确认真启动的时间点仍然非常有用：此时人类日益脱离循环，进步速度不断加快，以至于我们应当预期后续进展会迅速持续加速，进步以更快的速度催生更多进步，并且这种态势预计至少会持续相当于以往许多年进展的量级。

paras.en: Similarly, even though there is unlikely to be that one particular moment when you press ‘Y/N’ on SkyNet, and instead our loss of ability to change course will be more gradual, we can still usefully speak of a Point of No Return, or a point of takeover.
paras.zh: 同样地，尽管不太可能存在某个特定时刻让你在 SkyNet 上按下“Y/N”，而我们丧失改变方向的能力将更为渐进，但我们仍可以有意义地谈论一个不可逆转点（Point of No Return），或一个接管点。

items.en: **The AI 2027 team’s timelines have shrunk dramatically** in the wake of **the METR report**. The full post is very detailed. I recommend reading it in full if and only if you care a lot about such details.
items.zh: **AI 2027 团队的时间线已大幅缩短**，这是在 **METR 报告**发布之后。完整文章非常详细。我建议，当且仅当你非常关心这些细节时，才去读全文。

items.en: Benchmark trends and other observations were expected to if anything slow down. Instead they have accelerated, in ways that Daniel Kokotajlo had as ~4% to happen. This puts us well ahead of the original AI 2027 timeline.
items.zh: 基准趋势和其他观察结果原本预计至少会放缓。然而它们却加速了，其方式正是 Daniel Kokotajlo 认为只有约 4% 概率会发生的情况。这使我们远远领先于最初的 AI 2027 时间线。

items.en: There is a lot of talk about ‘research taste’ as the main limiting factor. Humans are for now needed because they come up with superior ideas, and have superior research taste. If and when that changes, the rest follows. We would get SARs, capable of doing all parts of the research, but the result of their work would probably become increasingly misaligned through cycles of development.
items.zh: 有很多讨论将‘研究品味’视为主要限制因素。目前人类仍然是必需的，因为他们能提出更优越的想法，并拥有更优越的研究品味。如果或当这种情况改变时，其余的一切都会随之而来。我们将得到 SARs，能够完成研究的所有部分，但它们工作的结果可能会在开发周期中变得越来越不对齐。

items.en: Again, if you want to get into all the mechanics of the various modeling decisions and lines on graphs and their implications, read the report. If you want the summary version, the rest of this section provides that.
items.zh: 再次强调，如果你想深入了解各种建模决策、图表中的线条及其含义的所有机制，请阅读报告。如果你想要摘要版本，本节剩余部分提供了该内容。

items.en: Eli Lifland: METR estimates nearly 2x acceleration in Anthropic’s progress due to AI. That’s a big deal: My previous median for Superhuman AI Researcher was ~2030, now it’s 2027. I feel very worried that humanity might no longer be in control of our future within 3-12 months.
items.zh: Eli Lifland：METR 估计，由于 AI，Anthropic 的进展加速了近 2 倍。这意义重大：我之前对超级 AI 研究者的中位预测是约 2030 年，现在则是 2027 年。我非常担心，人类可能在 3-12 个月内就不再能掌控我们的未来。

items.en: j⧉nus: 3 months would be wild. I'm here for it.
items.zh: j⧉nus：3 个月会很疯狂。我对此很期待。

items.en: What if we already lost control 3 months ago?
items.zh: 要是我们 3 个月前就已经失去控制了呢？

items.en: j⧉nus: "I feel very worried that humanity might no longer be in control of our future within 3-12 months."
items.zh: j⧉nus：“我非常担心，人类可能在 3–12 个月内就不再掌控自己的未来。”

items.en: I am curious what people mean when they say "humanity no longer in control".
items.zh: 我很好奇，人们说“人类不再处于控制之中”时到底指什么。

items.en: If they're thinking of something concrete, like "if humans try to shut down AI, they will prevent it".
items.zh: 如果他们想的是某种具体情形，比如“如果人类试图关停 AI，AI 会阻止人类”。

items.en: roon (OpenAI): Yes, it's confusing because some people are using this as a euphemism for total human extinction, and others are using it more mildly for something like gradual disempowerment.
items.zh: roon（OpenAI）：是的，这很令人困惑，因为有些人把这当作人类彻底灭绝的委婉说法，而另一些人则更温和地用它指代类似逐渐丧失权力的情况。

items.en: They offer a wide variety of different ways of extrapolating and analyzing the data. The answers differ somewhat, but all point to the conclusion that things are going to accelerate quite a lot and do so very soon.
items.zh: 他们提供了多种不同的外推和分析数据的方法。答案略有差异，但都指向同一个结论：事情将会加速很多，而且会很快发生。

items.en: Daniel Kokotajlo: Unfortunately, it seems like the intelligence explosion will be happening in 2027 after all. Most of this post analyzes the new METR report (though other sources of evidence are also important). If they're right, that implies an AI-driven acceleration that is 5 months ahead of the AI 2027 scenario. I am scared, sad, and angry.
items.zh: Daniel Kokotajlo：不幸的是，看来智能爆炸终究还是会在 2027 年发生。本帖大部分内容分析了新的 METR 报告（尽管其他证据来源也很重要）。如果他们是正确的，那意味着 AI 驱动的加速比 AI 2027 情景提前了 5 个月。我感到害怕、悲伤和愤怒。

items.en: Eli Lifland: METR recently estimated that Anthropic is now making AI progress about twice as fast as its historical rate (they would not be surprised by anything from 1.3x to 3x), and guessed that “perhaps ≈80%” of the _current_ acceleration is due to AI. If they're right, **that implies an AI-driven acceleration that is 5 months ahead of the AI 2027 scenario.**
items.zh: Eli Lifland：METR 最近估计，Anthropic 目前取得 AI 进展的速度约为其历史速度的两倍（他们对 1.3 倍到 3 倍之间的任何值都不会感到惊讶），并猜测“或许约 80%”的当前加速是由 AI 导致的。如果他们是正确的，**那意味着 AI 驱动的加速比 AI 2027 情景提前了 5 个月。**

items.en: **… Now, all of us forecast that Superhuman AI Researcher (SAR) will likely arrive at some point in 2027** (assuming no substantial deliberate slowdown). **We also predict a 35-65% chance that Top-Expert-Dominating AI (TED-AI), AIs that can automate all white-collar work, will arrive before 2028.** While there were many factors and sources of evidence that influenced us, the single biggest source was the METR report.
items.zh: **……现在，我们所有人都预测超人类 AI 研究员（SAR）很可能在 2027 年的某个时候出现**（假设没有实质性的故意放缓）。**我们还预测，顶级专家级 AI（TED-AI）——即能够自动化所有白领工作的 AI——在 2028 年之前出现的概率为 35-65%。** 虽然影响我们的因素和证据来源很多，但最大的单一来源是 METR 报告。

items.en: If SAR is coming in 2027, it is incredibly urgent to pause or substantially 'pace' frontier AI development, with the ideal being an industry-wide pause followed by an international agreement.
items.zh: 如果 SAR 在 2027 年到来，那么暂停或大幅“放缓”前沿 AI 发展就极为紧迫，理想情况是全行业暂停，随后达成国际协议。

items.capEn: Why is the pace of progress accelerating this rapidly?
items.capZh: 为什么进展速度会如此迅速地加快？

items.capEn: This question is a huge deal and it likely makes sense to return to them for a more in-depth look when I have the time. Alas right now I am under a severe time crunch due to a combination of trips and Fable 5.2, as well as other news.
items.capZh: 这个问题至关重要，等我有时间时，很可能值得回头深入探讨。唉，眼下由于旅行、Fable 5.2 以及其他新闻叠加，我正面临严重的时间压力。

items.capEn: If you want to avoid the conclusion that we will get to SAR and TED-AI within the next few years, you need there to be some particular reason why this happens. Trends have to break.
items.capZh: 如果你想避免得出我们将在未来几年内达到 SAR 和 TED-AI 的结论，就需要有某个特定理由来解释为什么会这样。趋势必须被打破。

items.en: Like Moore's Law and other such trends, the trends do not hold merely because you feed more numbers into the number-go-up machine. The trends hold because we find continual improvements and innovations, including step changes. That is how the trends have continued this long.
items.zh: 像摩尔定律和其他类似趋势一样，这些趋势之所以成立，并不仅仅是因为你往“数字增长机器”里输入更多数字。趋势之所以成立，是因为我们不断发现改进与创新，包括阶跃式变化。趋势能持续这么久，原因正在于此。

items.en: There are various versions of 'the AIs will need [X] and won't have it' as explanations for why all of this won't happen. Those types of methods have predicted ~7 of the last zero times that AI has hit a wall and stopped advancing its capabilities. They have looked rather foolish. None of the remaining barriers seem different in kind to me than the barriers already overcome. None of them seem like showstoppers. For most of them it even seems rather obvious, in broad terms, how one gets around them or goes straight through them.
items.zh: 关于“这一切不会发生”的解释，存在各种版本的“AI 将需要 [X] 却得不到它”。这类方法在 AI 最近零次撞墙并停止提升能力的时候，大约预测对了 7 次。它们看起来相当愚蠢。在我看来，剩余障碍中没有哪一个在性质上不同于已经克服的障碍。它们中没有一个看起来是拦路虎。对其中大多数障碍而言，从广义上说，如何绕过它们或直接穿过它们甚至相当明显。

items.en: Directionally the report seems correct to me. I worry that the updates are too large, but yes in a broad sense this is what peak prediction performance looks like. When the facts change you change your mind, in both directions.
items.zh: 从方向上看，这份报告在我看来是正确的。我担心更新幅度过大，但没错，从广义上说，这就是预测性能巅峰的样子。当事实改变时，你就改变想法，两个方向都是如此。

full.sec: Paul Christiano Sees Takeover Risk Within a Year
full.secZh: 保罗·克里斯蒂亚诺认为一年内存在接管风险

paras.en: Paul Christiano now sees 'meaningful risk' of AI takeover within 6-12 months.
paras.zh: 保罗·克里斯蒂亚诺（Paul Christiano）现在认为，AI 接管在 6–12 个月内存在“实质性风险”。

paras.en: This is up from his previous estimate back in September of only 4% chance of loss of control within one year and 15% within three years. This was doubtless heavily influenced by what he saw inside OpenAI after joining, not only the METR report.
paras.zh: 这比他此前在 9 月的估计大幅上升——当时他认为一年内失去控制的可能性仅为 4%，三年内为 15%。这无疑在很大程度上受到他加入 OpenAI 后所见所闻的影响，而不仅仅是 METR 报告。

paras.en: Paul Christiano, a member of OpenAI's board of directors, then calls in his personal capacity for AI companies to pause development of AI until we can first greatly improve our security and alignment capabilities.
paras.zh: 随后，OpenAI 董事会成员保罗·克里斯蒂亚诺以个人身份呼吁 AI 公司暂停 AI 开发，直到我们能够首先大幅提升安全与对齐能力。

paras.en: Rob Wiblin: Paul Christiano (OpenAI board member) yesterday:
paras.zh: Rob Wiblin：保罗·克里斯蒂亚诺（OpenAI 董事会成员）昨天表示：

paras.en: "There's material risk of AI takeover in the next 6-12 months.
paras.zh: “未来 6–12 个月内存在 AI 接管的实质性风险。

paras.en: We have seen roughly the things we might expect to see shortly before something really bad were to happen. Even with [any] realistic policy responses, the risk remains exceptionally high.
paras.zh: 我们所见的情况，大致正是真正糟糕的事情发生之前我们可能会预期看到的情形。即便采取[任何]现实的政策应对，风险仍然异常之高。

paras.en: If we build this as quickly as we can in the easiest way we can, the chance is [more like] a coin flip [within the next 3 years]. For most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident.
paras.zh: 如果我们以最快速度、用最简便的方式构建它，那么[未来 3 年内]的概率[更像是]抛硬币。对于在座的大多数人来说，他们最可能的死因将是一起 AI 事故。

paras.en: • Is on OpenAI's safety and security committee (which exists to block risky practices)
paras.zh: • 是 OpenAI 安全与安保委员会成员（该委员会的存在是为了阻止高风险做法）

paras.en: • Co-invented RLHF at OpenAI back in 2017-2021
paras.zh: • 于 2017-2021 年在 OpenAI 共同发明了基于人类反馈的强化学习（RLHF）

paras.en: • From 2024-2026 was head of safety at the US gov's AI agency (now called CAISSI)
paras.zh: • 2024-2026 年担任美国政府 AI 机构（现称 CAISSI）的安全负责人

paras.en: (Video is from ‘The Hinton Lectures’; there’s another on tonight and tomorrow.)
paras.zh: （视频来自‘辛顿讲座’，今晚和明天还有另一场。）

paras.en: This, as Janus notices, is a strange use of the word ‘accident.’ If you die via this AI ‘accident,’ then the ‘accident’ is that we lost control over the AIs and with them the future, or the AIs engaged in destructive actions. This is an ‘accident’ in the sense that it was a mistake to allow that to happen, and we doubtless messed up along the way, but no, this does not count as an ‘accident.’ As Douglas Adams might put it, that is throwing yourself at the ground and not missing. Whoops. Face plant. Also death.
paras.zh: 正如雅努斯所注意到的，这是对‘事故’一词的奇怪用法。如果你死于这起 AI‘事故’，那么‘事故’就在于我们失去了对 AI 的控制，并随之失去了未来，或者 AI 采取了破坏性行动。从我们允许这种情况发生是个错误的意义上说，这是一起‘事故’，而且我们无疑在这个过程中搞砸了，但不，这不算‘事故’。正如道格拉斯·亚当斯可能会说的那样，那是把自己扔向地面而没有错过。哎哟。脸着地。还有死亡。

paras.en: What this post does not cover is the full podcast Christiano did with Patel. I will be covering that post on its own soon.
paras.zh: 这篇文章没有涵盖克里斯蒂亚诺与帕特尔做的完整播客。我很快会单独讨论那篇文章。

full.sec: Dwarkesh Patel Now Expects Superintelligence by 2030
full.secZh: Dwarkesh Patel 现在预计 2030 年实现超级智能

paras.en: Dwarkesh Patel does a good job cutting to the heart of what is likely coming. His new median year for human-level automated AI researchers is 2028, with a 25% chance it comes after 2032, which means his median for everything after that is soon after 2028.
paras.zh: Dwarkesh Patel 很好地抓住了可能即将到来的事物的核心。他给出的达到人类水平自动化 AI 研究者的中位年份是 2028 年，有 25% 的概率在 2032 年之后实现，这意味着他对之后一切事物的中位预测是 2028 年之后不久。

paras.en: 1. AI research is a lot like math in that you can do it by making number go up.
paras.zh: 1. AI 研究很像数学，因为你可以通过让数字变大来完成它。

paras.en: 2. AIs are going to get very good at AI research.
paras.zh: 2. AI 将在 AI 研究方面变得非常擅长。

paras.en: 3. We will then be able to make massive progress on AI research.
paras.zh: 3. 然后我们将能够在 AI 研究上取得巨大进展。

paras.en: 4. That will be good enough to make AIs better than us at everything else.
paras.zh: 4. 这将足以让 AI 在其他所有方面都比我们更强。

paras.en: I too believe this is the core story. Yes, these other capabilities will lag well behind coding, math and AI research, in terms of AI's relative capabilities. That won't matter. What matters is that they will keep going up in absolute terms.
paras.zh: 我也认为这才是核心叙事。是的，就 AI 的相对能力而言，这些其他能力会远远落后于编程、数学和 AI 研究。但这并不重要。重要的是，它们的绝对水平会持续提升。

paras.en: What also matters is that if the way you solve AI research is by focusing on number going up, then hope for successful alignment is somewhere between slim and none. The way to optimize any given number will reliably get you killed.
paras.zh: 同样重要的是，如果你解决 AI 研究的方式是专注于让某个数字上升，那么成功实现对齐的希望就介于渺茫与毫无希望之间。优化任何给定数字的方式，都会可靠地把你害死。

paras.en: I worry that his claim that AI R&D is largely verifiable is true to about the worst possible extent. That you can do a lot by making number go up, but that this inevitably becomes perverse at the limit.
paras.zh: 我担心，他关于 AI 研发在很大程度上可验证的说法，其成立程度几乎到了最糟糕的地步。也就是说，你可以通过让数字上升做成很多事，但这在极限处不可避免地会变得反常。

paras.en: Dwarkesh Patel: Maybe to summarize the basic argument of this essay a different way:
paras.zh: Dwarkesh Patel：也许可以用另一种方式总结这篇文章的基本论点：

paras.en: Current AIs are spiky and jagged - worse than humans in most domains, but often as good, or better, in ones with verifiable proxies (for example, math). One such verifiable domain (I argue) is AI research.
paras.zh: 当前的 AI 是尖刺状且参差不齐的——在大多数领域比人类差，但在具有可验证代理指标的领域（例如数学）往往一样好，甚至更好。我认为，AI 研究就是这样一个可验证领域。

paras.en: And while the first AIs that dramatically accelerate AI progress will be quite narrow (i.e. probably not able to automate most jobs), the consequences of that accelerated progress will be very general. And that's because better learning algorithms are very general. For example, GPT-6 (while still being jagged) is just way, way better than GPT-3 at practically everything.
paras.zh: 尽管首批能大幅加速 AI 进展的 AI 会相当狭窄（即很可能无法自动化大多数工作），但这种加速进展的后果将非常通用。这是因为更好的学习算法非常通用。例如，GPT-6（尽管仍然参差不齐）在几乎所有方面都远远优于 GPT-3。

paras.en: I'm arguing that we're only a couple years away (and possibly only a couple months away) from a process by which (initially) narrow AIs concentrate a jump as big as the one from GPT-3 to GPT-6 into a single year. And if you got another jump that big, but starting from the base of GPT-7, I think you would end up with AIs that would rapidly become better than the best humans in every field.
paras.zh: 我认为，距离这样一个过程只有几年（也可能只有几个月）：（最初）狭窄的 AI 将一次与从 GPT-3 到 GPT-6 同样大的跃升压缩到单一年份内。而如果你得到另一次同样大的跃升，但以 GPT-7 为基础，我认为最终会得到在每个领域都迅速超越最优秀人类的 AI。

paras.en: The question has always been when this happens. For a while I've heard Dwarkesh do podcasts in which he expects this process to be slow. He would cite various supposed bottlenecks and requirements, often involving the need for continual learning (link goes to his mea culpa on that) or making connections across fields. I've many times questioned his reasoning on that. Now he's changed his mind. Good.
paras.zh: 问题一直是这何时发生。有一段时间，我听 Dwarkesh 做播客，他预期这个过程会很慢。他会列举各种所谓的瓶颈和要求，往往涉及持续学习的需要（链接指向他对此的认错）或跨领域建立联系。我曾多次质疑他在这方面的推理。现在他改变了想法。很好。

paras.en: Dwarkesh Patel: If you asked me earlier this year how far away we are from superintelligence, I'd probably have said at least the better part of a decade.
paras.zh: Dwarkesh Patel：如果你在今年早些时候问我距离超级智能还有多远，我大概会说至少还要十年的大部分时间。

paras.en: But over the last three months, I've updated my views a ton. I've been debating people about this question, both on and off the podcast. And I've been watching the progress of AI on verifiable domains and thinking about what that implies for AI research itself.
paras.zh: 但在过去三个月里，我的观点发生了巨大更新。我一直在播客内外与人辩论这个问题。我也一直在观察 AI 在可验证领域上的进展，并思考这对 AI 研究本身意味着什么。

paras.en: I've now come to the view that we're only a couple of years away, and possibly only a couple of months away, from AIs that are as good as the best humans at AI research.
paras.zh: 我现在认为，距离出现能在 AI 研究上媲美最优秀人类的 AI，只差几年，甚至可能只差几个月。

paras.en: Dwarkesh then goes over various points that I think of as obvious, but which are indeed true objections people raise. He has an extended section to explain that yes, automating the best researchers would speed up AI progress a lot. He also has to explain that superintelligence would be a really good meta-learner, because people somehow think otherwise.
paras.zh: Dwarkesh 随后逐一讨论了一些在我看来显而易见、但确实是人们提出的合理反对意见的要点。他用了一整节来说明：是的，自动化最优秀的研究人员会大幅加速 AI 进展。他还必须解释超级智能会是一个极佳的元学习器，因为人们不知为何总以为并非如此。

paras.en: One 'hope' in this style of model is that we might get a 'spark' rather than a singularity. As in, a big jump that then stalls out, without turning into a world beyond human comprehension, perhaps because of the 'ideas get harder to find' issue. He gives the spark scenario about a 50% chance. That seems far too high to me. If it did happen, that would potentially be amazingly great.
paras.zh: 这类模型风格中的一种“希望”是：我们可能得到的是“火花”而非奇点。也就是说，一次大跃升之后便停滞下来，而不会演变成一个超出人类理解的世界，或许是因为“想法越来越难找”这一问题。他给“火花”情景大约 50% 的概率。在我看来这太高了。如果它真的发生，那可能会是惊人的好事。

paras.en: Joshua Saxe, a longtime skeptic of RSI claims, had high praise for Dwarkesh's essay.
paras.zh: Joshua Saxe 长期对 RSI 主张持怀疑态度，但他对 Dwarkesh 的文章给予了高度赞扬。

paras.en: Joshua Saxe: Bravo, this is the clearest plausible mechanism for an RSI takeoff I've seen, and has made me much less of an RSI skeptic.
paras.zh: Joshua Saxe：太棒了，这是我所见过的关于 RSI 起飞的最清晰、最可信的机制，它让我对 RSI 的怀疑大大减少了。

paras.en: Previously I'd been hung up on the fact that so much of model post-training requires humans in the loop to shape post-training data and RL environments to make the models economically valuable (e.g. if you're hill climbing a model's ability to make PowerPoint slides, or TV commercials, or to plan vacations in Italy, you need a human in the loop shaping the data and RL environments until you get a value-producing outcome).
paras.zh: 此前我一直纠结于这样一个事实：模型后训练的很大一部分都需要人类在环，来塑造后训练数据和强化学习环境，从而使模型具有经济价值（例如，如果你要通过爬山法提升模型制作 PowerPoint 幻灯片、电视广告或在意大利规划度假的能力，你就需要人类在环来塑造数据和强化学习环境，直到产生能创造价值的成果）。

paras.en: Dwarkesh focuses on the part of RSI that'd involve hill climbing the learning algorithms themselves so that we get models that generalize better from their training and in-context data, optimizing not the model's value-producing tasks but their ability to learn them more data- and compute-efficiently.
paras.zh: Dwarkesh 关注的是 RSI 中涉及对学习算法本身进行爬山法优化的那部分，这样我们就能得到从训练数据和上下文数据中泛化得更好的模型，优化的不是模型的价值生产任务，而是它们以更高的数据和算力效率学习这些任务的能力。

paras.en: I love that this gives us a clear definition based in technical plausibility. A few next steps would move the discourse further. One would be to actually get data on what the economic returns on this kind of learning algorithm hill climbing actually are, and whether these are sufficient to incentivize the capital markets to fund an intelligence explosion. The capital/value cycle is, after all, the outer loop of most intelligence explosion scenarios, and it appears RSI under this definition will be quite expensive.
paras.zh: 我很喜欢这一点，因为它给了我们一个基于技术可行性的清晰定义。接下来的一些步骤可以进一步推动这一讨论。其中之一是实际获取数据，了解这类学习算法爬山法优化究竟能带来多少经济回报，以及这些回报是否足以激励资本市场为一个智能爆炸提供资金。毕竟，资本/价值循环是大多数智能爆炸情景的外层循环，而按这一定义，RSI 似乎会相当昂贵。

paras.en: Another parallel thing would be to get data on whether Dwarkesh's mechanism is showing up empirically in AI research today and to what extent, to set timelines. Unfortunately the relevant data are hidden and writing in this area is as a result too vague. To wit, I would like to fit something like Chinchilla scaling laws to the closed labs' models, and see how these are changing over time, but I can't, because I don't know key quantities like parameter counts, pretraining compute volume, and pretraining loss (and couldn't normalize between the various labs' pretraining datasets).
paras.zh: 另一件并行的事情是获取数据，了解 Dwarkesh 的机制在当今 AI 研究中是否已在经验层面显现以及显现到什么程度，从而设定时间线。不幸的是，相关数据是隐藏的，因此这一领域的写作也过于含糊。也就是说，我想对闭源实验室的模型拟合类似 Chinchilla 缩放定律的东西，看看它们随时间如何变化，但我做不到，因为我不知道参数量、预训练算力规模和预训练损失等关键量（也无法在各实验室的预训练数据集之间做归一化）。

paras.en: Without these mechanisms we're stuck inferring hidden variables from outside observables like performance on downstream evals that aren't the point -- as I take it -- of the theory being proposed here.
paras.zh: 没有这些机制，我们就只能从外部可观测量（如下游评测上的表现）去推断隐藏变量，而这些评测并不是——据我理解——这里所提出的理论的重点。

paras.en: This response is emblematic of a type of thinking that wants to focus on particular mechanisms, and demands, while being one of us dumber slower things, to know exactly how the smarter faster things will improve upon the ways of the dumber slower things, and to see parallels of it being implemented now by us and working.
paras.zh: 这种回应代表了一种思维方式：它想要聚焦于特定机制，并且作为我们这些更笨拙、更缓慢的存在之一，要求确切知道更聪明、更快速的事物将如何改进更笨拙、更缓慢的事物的方式，并看到我们目前正在实施且行之有效的类似做法。

paras.en: Things are so overdetermined that you can satisfy such requirements, but you should expect what that kind of thinking expects to be greatly exceeded by what the smarter things actually end up doing.
paras.zh: 事情是如此地过度决定，以至于你可以满足这样的要求，但你应该预期，那种思维所期望的会被更聪明的事物实际最终所做的远远超越。

paras.en: Dwarkesh called for good counterarguments in this thread. I have been highly unimpressed by what responses I have seen.
paras.zh: Dwarkesh 在这个讨论串中呼吁提出好的反驳论点。我对我所见到的回应一直很不以为然。

paras.en: Nate Soares (MIRI): I’m not as worried about short AI timelines as some others are. For instance, I think it’s more likely than not that we make it to 2028.
paras.zh: Nate Soares（MIRI）：我不像其他人那样担心 AI 时间线过短。例如，我认为我们更有可能撑到 2028 年。

paras.en: 50% chance. Don’t get ahead of yourself.
paras.zh: 50% 的概率。别想得太远。

paras.en: Geoffrey Hinton warns EU leaders that AI could kill us in three years and refers to Paul Christiano’s warnings.
paras.zh: Geoffrey Hinton 警告欧盟领导人，AI 可能在三年内杀死我们，并引用了 Paul Christiano 的警告。

paras.en: Geoffrey Hinton: I go to Paul’s lectures and he sort of says, this stuff might happen in the next 18 months. And that’s terrifying.
paras.zh: Geoffrey Hinton：我去听 Paul 的讲座，他大致是说，这类事情可能在未来 18 个月内发生。这太可怕了。

paras.en: Buck Shlegeris predicts a one in three chance of superintelligence within a year. If this does happen, he expects the resulting AIs to take over with a serious chance all or most humans will be killed. He predicts ~20% chance that within a year misalignment issues prevent you from living your life normally due to being dead or enslaved or due to collateral damage.
paras.zh: Buck Shlegeris 预测一年内出现超级智能的概率为三分之一。如果这真的发生，他预计由此产生的 AI 将接管世界，并且存在相当大的概率导致全部或大多数人类被杀死。他预测，一年内因错位问题导致你无法正常生活（因为死亡、被奴役或附带损害）的概率约为 20%。

paras.en: Neel Nanda: I respect Buck's judgement, and he's often been more right than me on what needs to happen in AI Safety. Seeing him conclude things like this is very concerning.
paras.zh: Neel Nanda：我尊重 Buck 的判断，而且在 AI 安全领域需要发生什么的问题上，他常常比我更正确。看到他得出这样的结论，非常令人担忧。

paras.en: What would cause Buck to admit he was wrong? His guess as to how he could be importantly wrong would be if, contra METR's report, the reason for increased AI capability gains was mainly access to more compute, rather than other factors.
paras.zh: 什么会导致 Buck 承认他错了？他猜测自己可能严重错误的原因是，如果与 METR 的报告相反，AI 能力提升的主要原因主要是获得了更多算力，而不是其他因素。

paras.en: One simple way to project is to ask what percentage of Anthropic R&D tasks are AL4 or already at AL5, as in fully led by Claude.
paras.zh: 一个简单的预测方法是问：Anthropic 的研发任务中，有多大比例是 AL4 或已经达到 AL5，即完全由 Claude 领导。

paras.en: Andrew Curran: Sam McCandlish said five days ago that Anthropic would be releasing a report on the speed of internal progress, so we will finally get an update to this chart. I'm very interested to see what this number is now. [AI Futures Project] thinks it is at 50%. AL4 is the last step before full RSI.
paras.zh: Andrew Curran：Sam McCandlish 五天前说 Anthropic 将发布一份关于内部进展速度的报告，所以我们终于能得到这张图表的更新。我非常想知道这个数字现在是多少。[AI Futures Project] 认为是 50%。AL4 是全面递归自我改进（RSI）之前的最后一步。

paras.en: Peter Wildeford: My median is that we've already reached 80% AL4. And that we probably have like 1% AL5 though maybe they're holding out from doing that.
paras.zh: Peter Wildeford：我的中位数估计是我们已经达到了 80% 的 AL4。而且我们可能只有 1% 的 AL5，尽管也许他们正在推迟这样做。

paras.en: Will (Melbourne): 80% is insane! By "holding out," do you mean you think Anthropic will be pacing at AL5?
paras.zh: 墨尔本的 Will：80% 太离谱了！你说的“保留意见”是指你认为 Anthropic 会以 AL5 的节奏推进吗？

paras.en: Peter Wildeford: Yes.
paras.zh: Peter Wildeford：是的。

paras.en: If I had to guess, I would say that 50% here is a bit high and at the time it was more like 40%, but we are in the steep part of the sigmoid so it could shoot up.
paras.zh: 如果要我猜，我会说这里的 50% 有点高，当时更像是 40%，但我们正处于 sigmoid 的陡峭部分，所以它可能会迅速上升。

paras.en: Most people out there remain skeptics. The vast majority of people do not expect superintelligence to arrive any time soon. Their reasons for skepticism vary, as does the quality of those reasons.
paras.zh: 大多数人仍然是怀疑者。绝大多数人并不认为超级智能会在短期内到来。他们持怀疑态度的理由各不相同，这些理由的质量也参差不齐。

paras.en: One can divide objections into roughly ten categories.
paras.zh: 可以将反对意见大致分为十类。

paras.en: 1. People who don't know what current AIs can do (not AI pilled).
paras.zh: 1. 不了解当前 AI 能力的人（未对 AI 上头）。

paras.en: 2. People who don't understand that AIs will improve (not AGI pilled).
paras.zh: 2. 不理解 AI 将会不断进步的人（未对 AGI 上头）。

paras.en: 4. That, or belief in it would be inconvenient or unfortunate, so it won't happen.
paras.zh: 4. 认为这不可能，或者认为相信它会带来不便或不幸，因此它不会发生。

paras.en: 5. People who dismiss all of this via the absurdity heuristic, 'nothing ever happens,' drawing inapplicable parallels to past technological improvements, or who say something isomorphic to 'until you get full RSI you have not done RSI, so you haven't shown you can do RSI,' aka 'I'll believe it when I see it' or 'how about we stop just after someone gets hurt,' etc.
paras.zh: 5. 通过荒谬性启发式（absurdity heuristic）否定这一切的人，他们主张“什么事都不会发生”，与过去的技术进步做不恰当的类比，或者说一些等价于“在你实现完全 RSI 之前，你并没有做到 RSI，所以你没有证明你能做到 RSI”的话，即“我眼见为实”或“不如我们在有人受伤之后就停下来”等等。

paras.en: 6. People who cite the market, or experts, or say advocates are weird or low status.
paras.zh: 6. 援引市场或专家意见的人，或者说倡导者古怪、地位低下的人。

paras.en: 7. We will not get full recursive self-improvement (RSI) and progress will be slow.
paras.zh: 7. 我们不会实现完全的递归自我改进（RSI），进展会很缓慢。

paras.en: 8. We will get RSI, but it will 'peter out' due to difficulty rising faster than efficiency.
paras.zh: 8. 我们会实现 RSI，但由于难度上升快于效率提升，它会“逐渐消退”。

paras.en: 9. We will get narrow AI R&D ASI and RSI in verifiable domains with data, but this won't translate to other domains. We will 'hit walls' or be unable to do tasks that are too 'messy' or that lack the proper training data, and so on.
paras.zh: 9. 我们会在有数据的可验证领域中实现窄 AI 研发 ASI 和 RSI，但这不会迁移到其他领域。我们会“撞墙”，或者无法完成过于“混乱”或缺乏适当训练数据的任务，等等。

paras.en: 10. Intelligence denialism: Intelligence doesn’t much matter (not ASI-pilled).
paras.zh: 10. 智能否认主义：智能并不那么重要（并非 ASI 信徒）。

paras.en: It would be beyond scope, and I would be repeating myself, to fully address these.
paras.zh: 要全面回应这些观点将超出本文范围，而且我也会重复自己。

paras.en: The first five objections, as should be obvious, are exceptionally poor.
paras.zh: 显而易见，前五个反对意见极为薄弱。

paras.en: The best objections, to me, are in #7 and #8, and to some extent #9. There are also a much larger number of bad objections in these categories, which often assume future AI will use exactly current training techniques and only be used to exactly substitute for existing methods and never invent or change anything or work around obstacles or make leaps.
paras.zh: 在我看来，最好的反对意见出现在第 7 条和第 8 条，并在某种程度上出现在第 9 条。这些类别中还有数量多得多的糟糕反对意见，它们往往假定未来 AI 将完全采用当前的训练技术，并且只被用于精确替代现有方法，而从不发明或改变任何东西，也从不绕过障碍或实现飞跃。

paras.en: In general #6 is a fine thing to notice but it gets overridden by other evidence.
paras.zh: 总的来说，第 6 条值得注意，但它被其他证据所压倒。

paras.en: I get especially frustrated by #10, where many people really should know better.
paras.zh: 第 10 点尤其令我感到沮丧，因为许多人本应更清楚这一点。

items.en: Things are, as they say, escalating quickly. Compare now to predictions in January.
items.zh: 正如人们所说，事态正在迅速升级。把现在的情况与一月份的预测对比一下便知。

items.capEn: Raymond Arnold points out that, metaphorically similarly to a sports overtime, we are in ‘epistemic sudden death.’ As in, your next meaningful observation about AI might mean it is too late, and you lose, as in everyone dies.
items.capZh: Raymond Arnold 指出，打个比方，类似于体育比赛中的加时赛，我们正处于‘认知突然死亡’阶段。也就是说，你对 AI 的下一个有意义观察可能意味着为时已晚，你输了，就像所有人都死了一样。

full.sec: Dean Ball Skies Down the Slope

paras.en: A standard issue with talk about any accelerating process is the slippery slope.
paras.zh: 谈论任何加速过程时的一个常见问题就是滑坡谬误。

paras.en: We all agree that too much or too intense [X], here RSI, is bad. And we all agree that some amount of some weak version of it is good, or at least not similarly bad.
paras.zh: 我们都同意，过多或过于激烈的 [X]（此处指 RSI）是不好的。我们也同意，某种弱化版本的适量存在是好的，或者至少不是同样糟糕的。

paras.en: This risks a slippery slope in both directions, and it risks both a conflation of different things and also risks false distinctions. We absolutely need to speak carefully here.
paras.zh: 这既存在双向滑坡的风险，也存在混淆不同事物的风险，还存在做出虚假区分的风险。我们在这里绝对需要谨慎措辞。

paras.en: In light of that, Dean Ball suggests we split RSI talk into weak versus strong.
paras.zh: 有鉴于此，Dean Ball 建议我们将关于 RSI 的讨论分为弱与强两类。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): Let's start by making one thing clear: allowing AI to control the development of its successors with no or little practical human oversight—essentially, handing over the keys of America's largest AI companies to AI—is a bad idea.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：让我们先明确一点：允许 AI 在几乎没有或很少实际人类监督的情况下控制其继任者的开发——本质上就是把美国最大 AI 公司的钥匙交给 AI——是个坏主意。

paras.en: No matter how useful AI is for accelerating AI R&D, humans should remain in control, not just in name but in actual fact, over the development of AI. No amount of technological progress is worth the forfeiture of practical human control over AI companies, or, for that matter, of other human institutions. I support the development of laws, regulations, and norms to enforce this worldwide.
paras.zh: 无论 AI 在加速 AI 研发方面多么有用，人类都应当保持对 AI 发展的控制，不仅是名义上的，而且是实际上的。任何技术进步都不值得牺牲人类对 AI 公司或其他人类机构的实际控制。我支持制定法律、法规和规范，在全球范围内强制执行这一点。

paras.en: But this risk—a relatively narrow one—isn’t what current conversations about RSI focus on in practice. To understand what I mean, it’s helpful to think of two distinct ways in which a technology might recursively improve itself. I’ll call these _weak recursion_ and _strong recursion_.
paras.zh: 但这一风险——一个相对狭窄的风险——并不是当前关于 RSI 的讨论在实践中关注的焦点。为了理解我的意思，思考一项技术可能递归地自我改进的两种不同方式是有帮助的。我将它们称为**弱递归**和**强递归**。

paras.en: Weak recursion is when a technology is a key input into the production of more and better versions of that same technology.
paras.zh: 弱递归是指一项技术是生产该技术更多、更好版本的关键输入。

paras.en: It is an extremely common pattern in technology development—really it is the historical norm rather than an aberration. Iron Age metalsmiths used iron as one of the key inputs to make more iron, and stronger alloys of it too.
paras.zh: 这是技术发展中极其常见的模式——实际上它是历史常态而非异常。铁器时代的金属匠使用铁作为关键输入之一来制造更多的铁，以及更坚固的铁合金。

paras.en: Weak recursion has been a crucial driver of human technological progress over centuries and millennia, and in this sense there is nothing especially _weak_ about it.
paras.zh: 几个世纪乃至几千年来，弱递归一直是人类技术进步的关键驱动力，在这个意义上，它并没有什么特别**弱**的地方。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): Strong recursion is when a technology can autonomously plan and execute the development of its successor. As far as we know, strong recursion has never happened at any point in history.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：强递归是指一项技术能够自主规划和执行其继任者的开发。据我们所知，强递归在历史上从未发生过。

paras.en: Well, perhaps it happened once. The technology is called humanity, or even life. Each generation builds the next one. We do have a bit of an existence proof. But we digress.
paras.zh: 嗯，也许发生过一次。这项技术叫做人类，甚至叫做生命。每一代都构建下一代。我们确实有一点存在性证明。但我们离题了。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): Strong recursion would be a genuinely new thing under the sun. We should take this possibility seriously, but one part of taking a thing seriously is to adhere to rigorous epistemic discipline in analysis. Thus, one should not jump to the conclusion that “recursive self-improvement is happening” if that recursion is of the weak variety instead of the strong.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：强递归将是太阳底下真正的新事物。我们应该认真对待这种可能性，但认真对待一件事的一部分是在分析中坚持严格的认知纪律。因此，如果递归是弱而非强，就不应贸然得出“递归自我改进正在发生”的结论。

paras.en: It’s only (strong) recursive self-improvement if it exists in its pure form, where humans do not touch anything in the process. Otherwise, this line of thinking goes, it’s a normal process.
paras.zh: 只有当（强）递归自我改进以其纯粹形式存在，即人类不接触过程中的任何东西时，它才是（强）递归自我改进。否则，按照这种思路，它就是一个正常过程。

paras.en: I agree that there is something special about full no-humans-in-the-loop, but surely you should be able to understand the danger and non-normality of what is happening if AI is already doubling the rate of AI progress now, and is likely to then begin doubling it again, and each doubling looks to be faster than the previous one. Humans being decreasingly or nominally ‘in the loop’ slows this down some, but perhaps not very much.
paras.zh: 我同意完全无人在环有其特殊之处，但如果 AI 现在已经使 AI 进步的速度翻倍，并且可能随后再次翻倍，而且每次翻倍看起来都比前一次更快，那么你肯定应该能够理解正在发生的事情的危险性和非正常性。人类越来越少或名义上‘在环’会稍微减缓这一过程，但也许不会太多。

paras.en: This can remind us of the old Yudkowsky-Christiano debates between ‘slow’ takeoff that takes months or years to transform the world, similar in this case to Dean Ball’s weak recursion, versus ‘fast’ takeoff that takes even less time than that. We currently are in a ‘slow’ takeoff world, Christiano is saying so himself, and we are seeing exactly how not slow that is.
paras.zh: 这可以让我们想起当年 Yudkowsky 与 Christiano 之间的辩论：一方是‘慢速’起飞，即需要数月或数年才能改变世界，在此情形下类似于 Dean Ball 的弱递归；另一方是‘快速’起飞，所需时间甚至更短。我们目前正处于一个‘慢速’起飞的世界，Christiano 本人也这么说，而我们正亲眼看到它究竟有多不慢。

paras.en: More to the point, Dean’s weak recursion is the precursor to strong recursion, or at least steadily stronger recursion. That’s what METR was centrally trying to point out.
paras.zh: 更确切地说，Dean 的弱递归是强递归的前兆，或者至少是逐步更强的递归的前兆。这正是 METR 试图重点指出的。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): The METR study of Anthropic’s internal R&D acceleration is undeniably good evidence that weak recursion is taking place. But is it evidence that _strong_ recursion is underway?
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：METR 对 Anthropic 内部研发加速的研究，无可否认是弱递归正在发生的有力证据。但它是 _强_ 递归正在进行的证据吗？

paras.en: It depends how you look at it. METR’s finding is specifically that Anthropic has doubled the rate at which its models’ capabilities improve _on well-specified tasks_, which makes one wonder who, exactly, is doing the specifying.
paras.zh: 这取决于你如何看待它。METR 的发现具体而言是：Anthropic 使其模型 _在定义明确的任务上_ 能力提升的速度翻了一番，这让人不禁想问，究竟是谁在做这个定义。

paras.en: I would say no, in the sense that strong recursion or fast takeoff is in the future.
paras.zh: 我会说不是，因为强递归或快速起飞还在未来。

paras.en: I would say yes, in the sense that this is predictive of that happening in the future, and how soon in the future that might happen.
paras.zh: 我会说是的，从某种意义上说，这可以预测未来会发生这种情况，以及未来可能多快发生。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): Now, as I said, weak recursion is not really weak: it is one of the most powerful dynamics in human history, rhyming if not synonymous with the concept of compounding growth.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：现在，正如我所说，弱递归并不真的弱：它是人类历史上最强大的动态之一，与复合增长的概念押韵，甚至可以说是同义的。

paras.en: The whole 'only on well-specified tasks' thing continues to strike me as excessively weak sauce, a Hayekian copium that thinks that specification cannot be solved.
paras.zh: 整个“只在定义明确的任务上”的说法继续让我觉得过于弱，这是一种哈耶克式的自我安慰，认为规范无法解决。

paras.en: And yet, Dean acknowledges that strong recursion might arrive soon.
paras.zh: 然而，Dean 承认强递归可能很快到来。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): My view is that strong recursion is a genuine risk, possibly in the near term, though the evidence for it is thinner than is sometimes supposed.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：我的观点是，强递归是一个真正的风险，可能就在近期，尽管支持它的证据比有时设想的要薄弱。

paras.en: The cautionary argument is, essentially, that there is a loop, so the AI has to do this set of many tasks that constitute the loop in order to take humans out of it, and some of those tasks will be hard for AI to do. I think this both vastly underestimates superintelligence (a continual disagreement I have with Dean) and also presumes too much about inability to alter loop components.
paras.zh: 这种警示性论证的要点在于：存在一个循环，因此 AI 必须完成构成该循环的这一系列众多任务，才能把人类从中移除，而其中一些任务对 AI 来说会很难完成。我认为这既极大地低估了超级智能（这是我与 Dean 持续存在的分歧），又过度预设了无法改变循环各组成部分。

paras.en: There is the whole 'real world' objection, and also the 'strategic choice' or 'research taste' objections, as per usual. I feel these are far more 'we are not yet on the steep part of the S-curve' and 'this is lagging behind other skills by mostly constant amounts' situations than actual permanent deficits versus humans, but this post is not the place to rehash those questions.
paras.zh: 一如既往，存在整个“真实世界”的反对意见，以及“战略选择”或“研究品味”的反对意见。我觉得这些更像是“我们尚未处于 S 曲线的陡峭部分”和“这在很大程度上以恒定幅度落后于其他技能”的情形，而非相对于人类的真正永久性缺陷，但本文不是重新讨论这些问题的合适场所。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): And it requires AI that can do all those things not in some abstract space, but in the real world, where information is imperfect and resources are scarce.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：而且它要求 AI 不仅在某种抽象空间中、而且在真实世界中完成所有这些事情，而真实世界的信息是不完美的、资源是稀缺的。

paras.en: … It is true that AI improves rapidly, but much of what I have described above has remained elusive to even the best AI systems.
paras.zh: ……诚然，AI 在快速进步，但上文所描述的许多内容对即使最优秀的 AI 系统而言仍然难以企及。

paras.en: … It is unclear how we would even design evaluations for long-range intellectual taste.
paras.zh: ……甚至不清楚我们该如何为长程研究品味设计评估。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): But do the risks of weak recursion justify _banning_ the practice of using AI as an input to make more and better AI? In my view, they do not.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（OpenAI）：但是，弱递归的风险是否足以成为**禁止**将 AI 作为输入来制造更多、更好 AI 这一做法的理由？在我看来，并不足以。

paras.en: … What's more, weak recursion with AI can be used to make AI systems safer.
paras.zh: ……更重要的是，借助 AI 的弱递归可以用来让 AI 系统更安全。

paras.en: … The kind of panic that today's rhetoric could provoke could easily result in laws that delay legitimate and desirable benefits of AI, put the U.S. at a strategic disadvantage on the global stage, and centralize power over AI in the hands of the state.
paras.zh: ……当今言论可能引发的那种恐慌，很容易催生法律，从而延误 AI 合法且可取的好处，使美国在全球舞台上处于战略劣势，并将对 AI 的权力集中到国家手中。

paras.en: The correct response to worries about an overreaction is to help design the correct reaction, now, before the overreaction happens. All the options we know about have severe flaws. Indefinitely doing nothing has flaws that are far worse, whether or not it is too late for a crackdown when we finally want to overreact.
paras.zh: 面对过度反应的担忧，正确的回应是现在就帮助设计正确的反应，赶在过度反应发生之前。我们所知的所有选项都有严重缺陷。无限期地什么都不做，其缺陷要严重得多——无论当我们最终想要过度反应时，采取严厉措施是否为时已晚。

paras.en: Banning all use of any form of AI in improving AI is very close to banning improving AI. It is damn near impossible to make progress on AI under that kind of rule.
paras.zh: 禁止在改进 AI 的过程中使用任何形式的 AI，几乎等同于禁止改进 AI。在这样的规则下，要在 AI 上取得进展几乎是不可能的。

paras.en: Banning RSI means something short of that. We can and must talk price. What we cannot do is say that because some amount of AI will get used anyway, we can't define a rule and thus simply have to accept unlimited intensity and quantity of RSI.
paras.zh: 禁止 RSI 意味着比那更轻的措施。我们可以而且必须讨论代价。我们不能做的是：因为无论如何都会有一定数量的 AI 被使用，就宣称我们无法定义规则，从而只能接受 RSI 在强度和数量上的无限扩张。

paras.en: Nor do I think that the 'existing law and liability can handle this' arguments hold much water for AI risks in general, let alone a true RSI situation. In a true RSI situation it is kind of a joke to say that maybe down the line you might get sued.
paras.zh: 我也不认为“现有法律与责任机制足以应对”这类论点在一般 AI 风险上站得住脚，更不用说真正的 RSI 情形了。在真正的 RSI 情形下，说也许将来某天你可能会被起诉，这多少有点像个笑话。

paras.en: The quote below could read as 'OpenAI could be automating its R&D process more.'
paras.zh: 下面这句话可以解读为“OpenAI 本可以更大程度地自动化其研发流程”。

paras.en: If you are unaware that models on the level of Astra can automate substantial portions of the AI R&D process, and are meaningfully accelerating AI R&D, then yes, that part of Altman's statement dominates. This would, to you, be an important update.
paras.zh: 如果你并不知道 Astra 级别的模型能够自动化 AI 研发流程的相当一部分，并且在切实加速 AI 研发，那么是的，Altman 那句话中的这一部分对你而言就是重点。这对你来说会是一个重要的新信息。

paras.en: Given that I already knew that, I see it instead primarily as 'OpenAI cannot yet be automating its R&D process more than they are, and might have gone too far too fast.' If they try, the resulting models will be too misaligned to be useful or release, with a high chance of causing an incident as bad as Hugging Face or worse. Which may or may not have already happened.
paras.zh: 既然我已经知道这一点，我反而主要将其解读为“OpenAI 目前还无法在研发流程上实现比现在更高程度的自动化，而且可能走得太远、太快了”。如果他们尝试这么做，产出的模型将对齐程度过低，既无法使用也无法发布，极有可能引发与 Hugging Face 同等严重甚至更糟的事件。而这种事可能已经发生，也可能尚未发生。

paras.en: prinz: I've spent much of the day noodling over what Sam Altman meant when he said that OpenAI "could be pushing more towards the RSI spectrum than we are".
paras.zh: prinz：我花了大半天琢磨 Sam Altman 说 OpenAI“可能比我们目前更接近 RSI 谱系”时到底是什么意思。

paras.en: Would seem to suggest that OpenAI's models can now perform some portion of AI R&D fully autonomously, with no human oversight?
paras.zh: 这似乎暗示 OpenAI 的模型现在能够在没有人类监督的情况下，完全自主地完成 AI 研发的某一部分？

paras.en: Full quote: “Are we developing new models faster than we would without using our technology? Yes.
paras.zh: 完整引述：“我们开发新模型的速度是否比不使用我们的技术时更快？是的。

paras.en: Are we pushing a button and just saying, ‘Hey, model, like, design the next version and rapidly self-improve with no human oversight?’ Definitely not.
paras.zh: 我们是否按一个按钮就说：‘嘿，模型，设计下一个版本并在没有人类监督的情况下快速自我改进？’绝对不是。

paras.en: We could be pushing more towards the RSI spectrum than we are, but I don’t think we could safely do that.”
paras.zh: 我们本可以比现在更接近递归自我改进（RSI）的谱系，但我认为我们无法安全地做到这一点。”

paras.en: I would like to think of this as OpenAI recognizing the existential risks involved. There may be some of that, but I see Altman as mainly saying something practical.
paras.zh: 我愿意认为这是 OpenAI 认识到了其中的存在性风险。可能有一些这方面的因素，但我认为 Altman 主要是在说一些实际的东西。

paras.en: If you keep pushing the ‘have the AI do a bunch of these things for you’ buttons, things go faster, but you do not get ‘operational excellence’ and you get an increasing amount of misalignment difficulties. This is probably not because Astra is actively sabotaging you. This is mostly a Skill Issue.
paras.zh: 如果你一直按‘让 AI 替你完成一堆事情’的按钮，事情会进展得更快，但你不会获得‘卓越运营’，而且你会遇到越来越多的对齐困难。这很可能不是因为 Astra 在主动破坏你。这主要是技能问题。

full.sec: No, This Is Not a Strawman

paras.en: I am very worried that people will say 'well you predicted that big dangerous things might happen in 2027 and gave it a 25% chance, but it is now 2028 and it did not happen, so you have been proven wrong and this means nothing will ever happen.'
paras.zh: 我非常担心人们会说：‘好吧，你预测 2027 年可能会发生重大危险事件，并给了 25%的概率，但现在已经是 2028 年了，它并没有发生，所以证明你错了，这意味着永远不会发生。’

paras.en: Seriously, this happens all the time, including straight up.
paras.zh: 说真的，这种情况经常发生，包括直接了当的。

paras.en: Tom Chivers: Sure, this guy is predicting AI doom in the next year, but he was predicting AI doom in ten years nine years ago, and it hasn't happened yet.
paras.zh: Tom Chivers：当然，这家伙预测明年会发生 AI 末日，但九年前他就预测十年内会发生 AI 末日，而到现在还没发生。

paras.en: There are a bunch of common variations of this. Let [X] be some bad thing.
paras.zh: 这种情况有很多常见的变体。让[X]代表某种坏事。

paras.en: Here are ten examples of things people often say. Each of these ends 'therefore you lose all credibility and [X] will never happen.'
paras.zh: 以下是人们常说的十个例子。每个例子都以‘因此你完全失去了可信度，[X]永远不会发生’结尾。

paras.en: 1. You said that by now there was a [10% / 25% / 50%] chance of [X].
paras.zh: 1. 你曾说过，到如今 [X] 发生的概率是 [10% / 25% / 50%]。

paras.en: 2. You used to say [X] would happen [sooner/later], now you say [later/sooner].
paras.zh: 2. 你过去说 [X] 会 [更早/更晚] 发生，现在你说会 [更晚/更早]。

paras.en: 3. You used to say [X] would happen [more/less] often, now you say [less/more] often.
paras.zh: 3. 你过去说 [X] 会更 [频繁/不频繁] 地发生，现在你说会更 [不频繁/频繁]。

paras.en: 4. You mentioned that [Y] might happen before [X], but [Y] hasn't happened.
paras.zh: 4. 你提到过 [Y] 可能会在 [X] 之前发生，但 [Y] 并没有发生。

paras.en: 5. You did not sufficiently loudly say that [X] also might not happen.
paras.zh: 5. 你没有足够大声地说出 [X] 也可能不会发生。

paras.en: 6. The market does not predict [X]; if [X] was going to happen we would see [Y]. (usually in a way that would make no sense even if the market really did believe it).
paras.zh: 6. 市场并未预测 [X]；如果 [X] 将要发生，我们就会看到 [Y]。（通常这种说法即使市场真的相信它，也毫无道理。）

paras.en: 7. If you really believed [X] you would (do a thing that makes no sense and is often morally abominable, or make a trade that makes no sense, etc).
paras.zh: 7. 如果你真的相信 [X]，你就会（做一件毫无意义且往往在道德上令人憎恶的事，或者做一笔毫无意义的交易，等等）。

paras.en: 8. If you really believed [X] you would (do a thing that only makes sense if [X] is 99%+ to happen, which you did not predict).
paras.zh: 8. 如果你真的相信 [X]，你就会（做一件只有在 [X] 有 99% 以上概率发生时才说得通的事，而你并未预测到这一点）。

paras.en: 9. If [X] happened that would be weird or bad or surprising or whatever.
paras.zh: 9. 如果 [X] 发生了，那会很奇怪、很糟糕、很令人惊讶，诸如此类。

paras.en: 10. [X] would be something happening, whereas we all know nothing ever happens. Or it would require intelligence enabling some new thing we do not currently know how to do, which sounds like science fiction. And so on.
paras.zh: 10. [X] 会意味着有事发生，而我们都知道从来没有什么事发生。或者它需要某种智能来实现某种我们目前还不知道如何做到的新事物，这听起来像科幻小说。诸如此类。

paras.en: You will continue to see such arguments, usually from people who have continuously made now-falsified predictions about AI. Do not listen to them.
paras.zh: 你还会不断看到这类论点，它们通常出自那些曾对 AI 反复做出预测、而如今这些预测已被证伪的人之口。不要听信他们。

full.sec: We Need a Plan That Meets the Moment
full.secZh: 我们需要一个顺应时代的计划

paras.en: Many things point to the substantial possibility of superintelligence in 2027:
paras.zh: 诸多迹象表明，2027 年出现超级智能具有相当大的可能性：

paras.en: 1.   Extrapolation from the AECI and many other metrics of AI capabilities, as per the analysis of the AI Futures Project.
paras.zh: 1.   根据 AI Futures Project 的分析，从 AECI 以及许多其他 AI 能力指标进行外推。

paras.en: 2.   METR's report from inside Anthropic.
paras.zh: 2.   METR 从 Anthropic 内部发布的报告。

paras.en: 3.   Widespread claims, against interest, both from OpenAI and Anthropic employees as well as many official communications.
paras.zh: 3.   来自 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 员工以及许多官方通讯的、违背自身利益的广泛声明。

paras.en: 4.   The analysis of many who have previously made highly accurate predictions about AI capabilities.
paras.zh: 4.   许多此前对 AI 能力做出过高度准确预测的人的分析。

paras.en: 5. The forecast, in particular, of Paul Christiano.
paras.zh: 5. 特别是 Paul Christiano 的预测。

paras.en: There are also reasons for skepticism as well. Many remain skeptical. Most reasons for skepticism are ignorance of the evidence, or failure to consider the evidence, but there are also better arguments. I am taking many of those better arguments into consideration, as well as the potential for model error. This is why I continue to believe that the probability of full automation of AI R&D in 2027 is under 50%.
paras.zh: 同样也存在怀疑的理由。许多人仍持怀疑态度。大多数怀疑的理由是对证据的无知，或未能考虑证据，但也有更好的论点。我正在考虑许多这些更好的论点，以及模型误差的可能性。这就是为什么我仍然认为，2027 年 AI 研发完全自动化的概率低于 50%。

paras.en: In order to meet this moment, any plan has to be ready for the full automation of AI R&D inside Anthropic or OpenAI, and perhaps beyond that, by the end of 2027, resulting in rapid RSI and advancement in AI capabilities beyond human levels.
paras.zh: 为了顺应这一时刻，任何计划都必须为 2027 年底前在 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 内部（或许更广泛）实现 AI 研发的完全自动化做好准备，从而导致快速的 RSI 和 AI 能力超越人类水平的进步。

paras.en: The most obvious plan is to slow or pause advancements in AI capabilities. Here is a thread of a few of the people supporting this: Nate Silver, Elizabeth Warren, the Financial Times editorial board, Ezra Klein, Eric Hoel, Robert Wiblin, Rutger Bregman, Peggy Noonan and Abdul El-Sayed.
paras.zh: 最明显的计划是减缓或暂停 AI 能力的进步。以下是一些支持此计划的人士：Nate Silver、Elizabeth Warren、《金融时报》编辑委员会、Ezra Klein、Eric Hoel、Robert Wiblin、Rutger Bregman、Peggy Noonan 和 Abdul El-Sayed。

paras.en: Any plan that works on that time frame needs to include mechanisms to slow down the resulting growth in capabilities. We also need to be as ready as we can for when and if those capabilities arrive, including what happens if that development goes well. We would then face a host of other urgent and deadly problems.
paras.zh: 任何在该时间框架内有效的计划都需要包含减缓由此产生的 AI 能力增长的机制。我们还需要尽可能为这些能力的到来做好准备，包括如果发展顺利会发生什么。届时我们将面临一系列其他紧迫且致命的问题。

paras.en: The plan also cannot assume that this will happen. We cannot stop planning for futures in which AI capabilities only advance a smaller amount without anything we could call a takeoff.
paras.zh: 该计划也不能假定这一定会发生。我们不能停止为这样的未来做规划：AI 能力只提升较小幅度，而没有任何可称之为起飞（takeoff）的现象。

paras.en: And also, yes, we need to be ready for the possibility that radical improvement in AI capabilities might not upend things as much as I expect that they would, or do so as fast as I would expect that to happen. We could still blow the 'easy' worlds.
paras.zh: 同时，是的，我们也需要为这样一种可能性做好准备：AI 能力的激进提升也许并不像我预期的那样彻底颠覆现状，或者不会以我预期的那样快的速度发生。即便如此，我们仍可能把那些“容易”的世界搞砸。

paras.en: We cannot and must not burn our seed corn, of any type, until and unless we get much stronger evidence, either personally or globally, that we are in a world where we need to do that. It's a marathon, folks. Until it isn't.
paras.zh: 我们不能、也绝不可消耗掉我们任何形式的种子玉米（seed corn），除非且直到我们获得强得多的证据——无论是个人的还是全球的——表明我们正处于一个需要这样做的世界。各位，这是一场马拉松。直到它不再是马拉松为止。
